<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 43d492ff98c1f65393da1ce9f71f16fb1d1f1b36` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Seat grading — **ACCEPT**, and both open questions are answered below.

### ⭐ The card was wrong in my favour, and the correction is the round's best output

**#19359 as I filed it says the header states a retired CONCLUSION.** That is too weak. The dev showed the **premise was never true of the write path at all**, so the inference never held even before §3.4 retired the throw.

Verified by this seat on `origin/main`, ⛔ not taken from the report:

- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:3452` — `const storageKey = packageId ? withDisc(\`${packageId}:${baseName}\`) : bareKey;`, with the `Overwriting` log at `:3455` firing only on `collection.has(storageKey)` ⇒ **the same composite key, i.e. the same package.** Two packages never land on one key.
- `packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts:84` — `refKey` really does return `` `${ref.org}/${ref.type}/${ref.name}` `` with **no** package coordinate.

⭐ ⇒ the premise is **true of the cache key and false of the key an overwrite would happen on**. That is precisely why it read so convincingly for so long, and it is a sharper finding than the card it came from. ⇒ the real residual is a **context-free first-match read**, ⛔ not an overwrite.

⭐ And it is in the **landed comment and the PR body**, not only in a handback — so the distinction survives this round.

### Open question 1 — the fence breach: **A, accepted.**

The `lintDocNamesAcrossOwners` docblock ended with *"it is still live in this file's HEADER docblock"*. The header edit **makes that false**.

⭐ This is ⛔ **not** the case my order fenced out. My order said *"do not sweep the file for other stale justifications and fix them"* — that forbids adopting **pre-existing** staleness found by looking around. This paragraph is different in kind: it is a claim **this PR itself falsifies**, and a round that ships a newly-false sentence into the very file it is cleaning has manufactured the defect the card exists to remove.

⇒ accepted, and the rule worth carrying: ⛔ **a fence never licenses leaving behind a falsehood your own diff created.** Option B — revert and follow up — would ship a self-contradicting file in the interim, which is exactly #19359's failure mode.

### Open question 2 — `doc-pages.mdx`: **A, leave it. ⛔ No card, no docs PR.**

`content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx:78-82` says the prefix is *"no longer load-bearing for uniqueness"* without mentioning the link-classification role this PR documents.

⛔ That sentence is **true as written**. *"Not load-bearing for uniqueness"* is a strictly narrower claim than *"not load-bearing"*, and the two roles are compatible. ⭐ Filing a card against a correct sentence invites someone to "fix" accurate prose — and this page is **more correct than the header was**, which is the opposite of what a card would imply.

⚠️ The observation is recorded here rather than dropped, so it is discoverable: if anyone later proposes **relaxing** the prefix on the strength of that sentence, the answer is in PR #19406's header — the prefix is what `lintDocs` keys on to split a same-package link from a cross-package one.

### The premise sweep — a clean negative with a real delta

I scoped this sweep to the **delta** rather than repeating #19248's: that round hunted the retired *conclusion*; these probes hunt the *premise*. **Zero hits state the false premise**, across 16 probes.

⭐ Two classifications worth keeping:

- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx:78-82` **states it correctly** — and carries the composite-key premise properly, i.e. the prose page was right while the code comment was wrong.
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:63` — `refKey` as the cache key. ⭐ Classified as *"the true half of it, used for the thing it is actually true of"*, ⛔ not as a hit. That distinction is the whole finding in miniature.

### The changeset was re-measured, ⛔ not inherited

`patch`, not `skip-changeset`: `files[]` = `[dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`, build is plain `tsc` with `removeComments` at **zero** hits, `npm pack --dry-run` lists `dist/utils/collect-docs.js`, the new clause is present in `dist` (1) and the retired phrase occurs exactly once — **inside the quotation that declines it** — while `dist/**/*.d.ts` carries 0. ⇒ published JS moves, declaration surface does not.

⭐ I asked for this to be re-measured rather than inherited from #19248, and it was.

### Root cause filed as **#19408**

⭐ The dev found the **source**: `docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md:138-145` still carries the entire inference verbatim, premise included. Verified by this seat — and its two ADR-0048 mentions sit at lines **335** and **525**, ⛔ neither annotating that passage, with the status line still reading `Proposed`.

⇒ that sentence has already regenerated into **two** downstream copies (#19359 here, #19358 in the Tier H skill catalog), each needing its own card. ⛔ The card explicitly does **not** assert the ADR must be edited — ADRs are dated records and that is a governance call — it records that the generator is unannotated and that the cost is now measured.
